mcq.question: Why does `Battle` take a seed and own its `std::mt19937` instead of using `std::random_device` directly?

options.B: So that the same seed replays exactly the same battle, which makes the game testable
options.C: Because `mt19937` is required for `uniform_int_distribution` to compile

mcq.explanation: Injecting the source of randomness turns a non-deterministic game into a reproducible one. Tests fix the seed; the real game can still seed from `random_device`.

mcq.question: How does `Ogre` change the way it attacks?

options.A: It changes a global damage table
options.B: It hides `roll_damage` with a non-virtual function of the same name
options.C: It overrides the virtual `roll_damage` and sometimes returns 0 before calling the base version
options.D: It adds a new data member that `Battle` checks

mcq.explanation: The battle calls `roll_damage` through a `Monster&`, so the override is chosen at run time. The base class implementation is reused for the actual hit.

bonus.question: Many games use an entity-component-system design instead of an inheritance hierarchy. What problems of deep hierarchies does ECS avoid?
Write a failing test for a `Skeleton` monster that takes half damage from attacks, then implement it by overriding a new virtual `take_hit` in `Combatant`.
